question: Most seawater has about how much salt in every 1,000 g (about a litre) of water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**35 g**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **35 g** of salt is typically found in every 1,000 g (about a litre) of seawater.
 
• Seawater's salinity is a measure of the concentration of salts dissolved in it, primarily sodium chloride.
 
• The average salinity of seawater is about **3.5%**, which means 35 g of salt per litre.
